structured_output.summary: The law gives 0. Under federal law, NC Medicaid can cover children aged 6–18 between 133% and 211% FPL only through the CHIP-funded optional targeted low-income child (OTLIC) group, and that group excludes any child covered under a group health plan. The prompt states that Child 2 has employer-sponsored insurance, so the only group left is 435.118, capped at 133% FPL (138% with the 5-point disregard). Child 2's MAGI of $82,301 is about 212.8% of the 2026 FPL ($38,680 for 5), far above that cap. The engine tested only income against NC's 211% older-child limit and found eligibility, ignoring the no-other-coverage condition. So the reference of 1 misapplies the law, and the 44-model consensus of 0 is correct.
structured_output.engine_step_at_issue: The OLDER_CHILD category check: the engine found Child 2 eligible because MAGI of 2.13× FPL is within NC's 211% (with disregard) children's limit. It did not apply the OTLIC / targeted low-income child rule that the 133–211% band for ages 6–18 excludes children covered under a group health plan. The input that Child 2 has employer-sponsored insurance was never used.
